name: Three-Bar Play
note: Ignition, hold, release. Bar 1 is a repricing event: range at least ign_atr x ATR(14), close in the top (or bottom) loc_min of its own range, volume at least vol_mult x the 20-bar average. Bar 2 is the measurement of acceptance: it must stay inside bar 1, give back no more than `giveback` of bar 1's range, be no wider than r2_cap of it, and trade less volume. The trade is the release -- bar 3 taking out bar 2's extreme, valid on that one bar only. Short setup is the exact mirror. The stop-order entry becomes a close-of-bar-3 decision filled at bar 4's open, because that is the only honest way this harness can fill it.
source: Bellafiore, M. (2010), 'One Good Trade' and SMB Capital training material, where the 'three bar play' is taught as an ignition bar, a small consolidation bar, and a break of the consolidation bar's high. Published as a discretionary pattern with no numeric thresholds; the range multiples, close-location floor, give-back cap and volume ratios above are my quantification so that it can be backtested at all.
